title: Security Ask Ontology and Routing Heuristics
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define a formal, machine-friendly ontology and routing heuristics for incoming security and compliance asks (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA, vendor questionnaires) so requests are classified, prioritized, and routed automatically to the correct team or escalation lane. This ticket captures scope for taxonomy design, a lightweight classifier + thresholding, routing rules, UI affordances for CS/legal, and metrics to validate. Aim: reduce manual triage volume and time-to-first-response while preserving conservative human review for high-risk items.
goals: Establish a canonical taxonomy (20-30 labels) covering data residency, encryption/KMS, access controls, audit logs, breach notification, third-party subprocessors, HIPAA PHI controls, GDPR lawful basis/DPA clauses, SOC2 control families, and questionnaire categories.
Deliver routing heuristics that map labels + risk score -> lane (auto-respond, CS-first, legal review, security ops escalation).
Prototype a classifier with >=85% macro-F1 on held-out historical intake examples and thresholding to maintain precision >=90% for 'legal review' lane.
Integrate with Linear intake form and CS internal console so 60% of inbound asks are routed automatically within 2 weeks of rollout, with audit trail.
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy document published in Confluence and approved by Legal/Security/CS leads.
Classifier model trained on labeled historical tickets and evaluated; metrics (precision/recall/F1) documented and reviewed.
Routing rules implemented in intake pipeline; automated tests exist for rule coverage >=90% of top 100 historical request types.
CS console displays predicted labels, confidence, and single-click override that creates a routed Linear issue with correct metadata.
SLOs: median time-to-route < 1 hour, first human triage time for routed tickets < 8 hours for high-risk lanes.
Monitoring dashboard with weekly automated drift checks and human review workflow for misrouted items.
success_metrics: Percent of inbound security asks auto-routed: target 60% after 4 weeks
Reduction in manual triage volume (CS + Security): target 40% within quarter
proposed_workflow: 1) Customer or AE submits intake form -> 2) Preprocessor extracts text fields and attachments (questionnaire PDFs) -> 3) Classifier predicts labels and risk score -> 4) Routing heuristics map (labels, score, customer segment, contract status) to lane -> 5) Create Linear ticket with populated metadata and evidence bundle, or auto-send templated response for low-risk items -> 6) Human-in-loop review panel shows predictions and override action; overrides feed back as labeled examples for retraining.
classifier_spec: Model: lightweight transformer or logistic regression ensemble for speed; input features: title, body, attachment OCR text, customer tags (enterprise, region), previous ticket history, past escrow/contract flags. Labels: multi-label (e.g., 'DPA: data transfer', 'SOC2: logging', 'HIPAA: BA agreement required', 'Questionnaire: VendorRisk - Security'). Outputs: label probabilities and an overall risk score (0-100). Thresholding: conservative high-risk threshold for auto-escalation to Legal/Security, permissive low-risk threshold for auto-response. Training data: sample ~5k historical intake tickets labeled by Security/Legal. Evaluation: stratified cross-val; track per-label precision/recall; target macro-F1 >=0.85. Monitoring: weekly accuracy sampling, trigger retrain when drift > 8% or confidence distribution shifts. Data retention: follow privacy retention policy; training data redacted for PHI.
routing_heuristics: If label includes 'HIPAA' or 'PHI' and customer is enterprise -> route to Security Ops + Legal (high-risk lane)
If label probability for 'DPA: international transfer' > 0.7 and customer region EU -> route to Legal DPA reviewer
If label matches 'SOC2: minor control clarification' and contract tier is standard -> route to CS with templated answer
If incoming ticket is a vendor questionnaire attachment and checksum matches known large vendor -> create Evidence bucket, assign to Compliance Ops
If classifier confidence < 0.5 -> assign triage to human CS for classification
Map contract status: if NDA or custom DPA present -> escalate faster and mark priority
Allow manual override to 'urgent' or 'legal review' by CS or AE, which updates ticket metadata and increments training data label.
escalation_playbook: High-risk hit (HIPAA PHI / data breach report / active exploit) -> Immediately create SEV ticket, notify on-call Security (Slack #sec-oncall), and page Legal on-call.
DPA clause dispute escalated by Sales -> Legal owns formal response; CS provides evidence pack and contract snapshot within 48 hours.
Missed SLA: if first-response > SLA and customer_impact=high -> auto-create incident review item and notify PM and CS leadership.
Quarterly review: top 50 misrouted tickets examined; taxonomy updates scheduled into backlog.
ui_changes: CS console: show predicted labels, risk score, top 3 evidence snippets, link to uploaded questionnaire; buttons: 'Approve Routing', 'Escalate to Legal', 'Auto-Respond', 'Override & Label'. Linear ticket template must include fields: taxonomy_labels (list), classifier_confidence, routed_lane, customer_tier, evidence_links.
integration_points: Confluence taxonomy + training data labeling guide: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFERENCE/Security+Ask+Ontology
Internal drive: evidence bundle templates and response templates: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1AbC...
tasks: Taxonomy design workshop (invite Legal, Security, CS) - 2pts
Label 5k historical items and build goldset - 3pts
Implement routing rules in intake pipeline and tests - 5pts
CS console UI changes and override button - 3pts
Run pilot with 2 enterprise customers and measure - 2pts
notes: Trade-off: aggressive auto-routing reduces queue but increases risk of misrouted sensitive asks; mitigate via conservative thresholds and quick override UX.
We should prioritize explainability (top tokens, matched clause snippets) in UI so Legal trusts the classifier outputs.
Consider attaching redaction step for attachments containing PHI before they are used for training.
Revisit taxonomy quarterly; keep it intentionally small to start (20-30 labels) to avoid low-signal classes.
